quizName: DMV Practice Test #12 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: When should you flash your brake light?

options.text: When you are tired while riding.
When you will slow down where other drivers won't expect it.
When there is a stop sign ahead.
When your signals are not working.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you will slow down where other drivers won't expect it.
questions.explanation: Motorcycle brake lights are hard to see compared to car brake lights. Flashing your brake light helps other drivers notice you are stopping. Flash your brake light before you slow down unexpectedly, such as in the middle of a block or near an alley.

questions.question: What should passengers do on a motorcycle?

options.text: Lean with the rider.
Never touch the rider.
Sit as far back as possible on the seat.
Hold onto the seat.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lean with the rider.
questions.explanation: Tell your passenger to lean with you during turns and curves. The passenger should hold onto your waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: What should you do if your motorcycle starts to wobble?

options.text: Shift to a lower gear.
Speed up.
Hold the handlebars firmly and slowly close the throttle.
Slowly apply the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the handlebars firmly and slowly close the throttle.
questions.explanation: Do not speed up when your motorcycle wobbles. This makes it worse. Instead, grip the handlebars firmly and slowly close the throttle to slow down. Move your weight forward and down. Pull off the road as soon as you can. Do not use the brakes, as this can make the wobble worse.

questions.question: How should you ride over an obstacle in the road?

options.text: Approach it at a 90-degree angle as much as possible.
Try to hit only the side of the obstacle.
Speed up before hitting the obstacle.
Lean the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Approach it at a 90-degree angle as much as possible.
questions.explanation: If you cannot avoid an obstacle, approach it at a 90-degree angle. Slow down, keep your motorcycle straight, rise slightly off the seat, and roll on the throttle just before you hit it.

questions.question: What is true about more than half of all motorcycle crashes?

options.text: They happen at speeds greater than 35 mph.
They happen at night.
They are caused by worn tires.
They involve riders with less than six months of experience on that motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: They involve riders with less than six months of experience on that motorcycle.
questions.explanation: More than half of all motorcycle crashes involve riders who have ridden that motorcycle for less than six months.

questions.question: How do you lean a motorcycle to turn?

options.text: Press the handgrip in the direction you want to turn.
Press the handgrip in the opposite direction of the turn.
Apply the front brake.
Apply the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the handgrip in the direction you want to turn.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle must lean to turn. To make the motorcycle lean, press the handgrip in the direction you want to turn.

questions.question: What is a sign that a motorcycle fits you properly?

options.text: You can touch the ground with your feet while seated.
The seat is even with your waist.
The seat is 10 inches above your waist.
The seat is 10 inches below your waist.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can touch the ground with your feet while seated.
questions.explanation: A properly-fitted motorcycle allows you to touch the ground with your feet while you are seated. When riding, keep your feet firmly on the footrests.

questions.question: What happens if your front tire goes flat while riding?

options.text: The steering will feel heavy.
The steering will feel loose.
The steering will not change.
The ride will feel too smooth.

questions.correctAnswerText: The steering will feel heavy.
questions.explanation: A flat front tire makes the steering feel heavy. If your steering feels heavy, exit the road right away and check your tires.

questions.question: Where should you position your motorcycle when being passed from behind?

options.text: Move onto the shoulder.
Use the left portion of your lane.
Use the center portion of your lane.
Use the right portion of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the center portion of your lane.
questions.explanation: When being passed, the center of your lane is the safest position. Riding on the side closest to the passing vehicle risks a collision. Riding on the far side may cause the driver to swerve back into your lane before it is safe.

questions.question: What should you do before carrying a passenger in traffic for the first time?

options.text: Read books about carrying passengers.
Practice riding on an empty road.
Flash your lights so others can see you.
Practice riding on the shoulder of a road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Practice riding on an empty road.
questions.explanation: Before carrying a passenger or heavy load in traffic for the first time, practice on a quiet road. This helps you get used to how your motorcycle handles with the extra weight.

questions.question: When entering a turn, a rider should:

options.text: Speed up.
Slow down.
Lean their shoulders to match the turn angle.
Sit as upright as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Before turning, slow your motorcycle by releasing the throttle and using both brakes if needed.

questions.question: When riding downhill on a motorcycle with a sidecar:

options.text: Stopping will be easier than without a sidecar.
Stopping will take longer than without a sidecar.
You cannot stop.
Stopping is about as easy as without the sidecar.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stopping will take longer than without a sidecar.
questions.explanation: A sidecar adds weight to your motorcycle, which means you need more braking power to stop. Stopping takes longer going downhill than on flat ground.

questions.question: If your motorcycle begins to wobble, you should:

options.text: Keep riding. The wobble will likely stop on its own.
Brake hard.
Release the throttle to slow down.
Speed up quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the throttle to slow down.
questions.explanation: Speeding up will make wobbling worse. Instead, grip the handlebars firmly, slowly release the throttle to slow down, move your weight forward and down, and pull off the road as soon as possible to check what is causing the wobble.

questions.question: Riding directly alongside another vehicle is discouraged because:

options.text: You may have trouble reaching a highway exit.
You may be in the other vehicle's blind spot.
You may block the driver's view.
It stops other drivers from passing both of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may be in the other vehicle's blind spot.
questions.explanation: Riding alongside another vehicle is dangerous because you might be in their blind spot. The driver could change lanes without seeing you. Also, the vehicle blocks any escape route if a hazard appears.

questions.question: When riding on a slippery surface, you should:

options.text: Speed up.
Make sudden moves.
Move to the edge of the road.
Follow the tire tracks left by cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Follow the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: Safe riding on slippery surfaces means slowing down, avoiding sudden moves, staying away from the road edge, and following the tire tracks left by other vehicles.

questions.question: What should a rider do to prevent injury on a slippery surface?

options.text: Speed up.
Slow down.
Make sudden moves.
Ride on the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Reduce your speed on slippery surfaces to stay safe. Sudden moves on slippery roads can cause your motorcycle to skid. Do not use the shoulder to avoid slippery roads.

questions.question: When carrying a load in a sidecar, you should:

options.text: Let the load move freely.
Secure the load so it does not shift.
Place the load loose in the seat.
Secure the load near the front of the sidecar.

questions.correctAnswerText: Secure the load so it does not shift.
questions.explanation: Secure all loads in a sidecar so they do not move and affect how your motorcycle handles. Place loads toward the rear of the sidecar to prevent the sidecar from tipping forward during sharp left turns.

questions.question: Many over-the-counter drugs:

options.text: Make riding more dangerous.
Make riding safer.
Only affect your riding if you drink alcohol too.
Affect everyone the same way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make riding more dangerous.
questions.explanation: Many drugs—including prescription medications, over-the-counter medications, and illegal drugs—have side effects that can affect your ability to ride safely, just like alcohol does.

questions.question: If a tire goes flat while riding, you should:

options.text: Open the throttle.
Hold the handlebars loosely.
Gently brake on the tire that is not flat.
Speed up to leave the road quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Gently brake on the tire that is not flat.
questions.explanation: If a tire goes flat, release the throttle and keep riding straight as you slow down. If you must brake, gently use the brake of the tire that is still good.

questions.question: When slowing or stopping, you should use both brakes:

options.text: Only when the pavement is wet.
Rarely.
Only in the city.
Every time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Every time.
questions.explanation: Using both the front and rear brakes gives you the strongest stopping power. Use both brakes every time you slow down or stop.

questions.question: Most crashes happen during the day. What should you do to reduce your chance of crashing?

options.text: Wear dark-colored clothing.
Wear bright-colored clothing.
Do not ride during the day.
Find safer routes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear bright-colored clothing.
questions.explanation: Wear bright-colored clothing to make yourself easy to see. This reduces your crash risk, even during the day.

questions.question: When using the front brake, you should:

options.text: Squeeze the lever smoothly and increase pressure gradually.
Grab the brake with only two fingers.
Press down on the brake lever with your foot.
Stomp on the brake lever hard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Squeeze the lever smoothly and increase pressure gradually.
questions.explanation: Use all four fingers to squeeze the brake lever firmly and smoothly. Apply more pressure slowly to stop safely.

questions.question: Which type of sign is yellow with black letters or symbols?

options.text: Warning
Service
Regulatory
Speed limit

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They alert drivers to dangerous road conditions ahead.

questions.question: If a tire goes flat while riding, the best thing to do is:

options.text: Relax your grip on the handlebars.
Shift your weight toward the good tire.
Brake on the good tire and steer to the roadside.
Use both brakes and stop quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake on the good tire and steer to the roadside.
questions.explanation: Hold the handlebars firmly and slow down by releasing the throttle. Brake gently on the working tire. Move toward the roadside as you slow down, then stop.

questions.question: A motorcycle horn should be used:

options.text: Never.
All the time.
When you think someone might move into your lane.
Not at all, it does not work.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you think someone might move into your lane.
questions.explanation: Use your horn to get a driver's attention quickly. Use it when another driver is moving into your lane unsafely or in any emergency situation.
